User says Expensify does 'pretty horrible categorization'. It is very good at reading the amount, but gets the category wrong about 70% of the time unless it's obvious, like Uber. Example: after they classified a United WiFi charge, it labeled their next airplane tickets as 'WiFi'.
User says Expensify took about 20 minutes to process a few receipt images, so they ended up entering the data themselves anyway.

Commenter says their wife does Mechanical Turk work and around Nov 20 saw many Expensify receipt tasks. Some receipts had enough info to identify people, such as store card numbers and buyer phone numbers.

User says Expensify's mobile app offers no apparent way to opt out of SmartScan. They believe phone bills and an exchange screenshot submitted for reimbursement were seen by MTurk workers. They tie this to a targeted SIM-port attack that nearly cost them $30k in bitcoin, and call the data handling 'reckless'.
Commenter says Expensify's 'Concierge' service is actually human-powered, citing a reply that said 'our team usually responds within 24 business hours (7am - 6pm)'.
After their startup was acquired, user had to move from Expensify to SAP Concur: 'Lord, how I miss Expensify. It was the epitome of intuitive.'
User says Expensify is 'so much nicer to use' than SAP Concur when you track your own expenses. They love that it scans receipts and enters the data for you.

Admin says Expensify raised their bill incrementally but substantially over eight months with no notification. Support said they weren't notified because they had opted out of marketing emails, and refused a credit. When threatened with cancellation, Expensify didn't care, so the company replaced it. 'The product was ok.'

User finds data entry 'unnecessarily painful'. Pressing Enter on the vendor autocomplete saves the whole expense and exits to the list, while Enter accepts autocomplete in other fields. They call the behavior inconsistent and say nobody on the web team seems to care.

User says Expensify's CEO emailed everyone Expensify had an address for, including employees who only submit expenses, urging a vote for Biden before the 2020 election. 'I will never give this company a single cent after that stunt.'

Commenter says the CEO's election email also went to foreign customers and calls it 'gross misuse of customer data'. Another says their workplace had no US employees, yet everyone got the email telling them how to vote, which they found very strange.
